2. Ghost-Anteile im Double-Tap-Modus vollständig unterdrückt

_**Agent (gpt-5.3-codex 2026-03-04 07:52:02Z)**_

`stale` kommt vom String-Catalog-Metadatum, nicht vom Widget-Text selbst.

In [Localizable.xcstrings](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataruWidgets/Localizable.xcstrings:200) steht beim Key `"Show ${device}"`:

- `"extractionState": "stale"`

Das bedeutet: Xcode hat beim letzten String-Extract keinen aktuellen Source-Match für diesen Key gefunden (veralteter Extract-Eintrag).  
Darum taucht die Änderung auch als Git-Diff auf.

Ursache hier: der Key gehört zur AppIntent-`Summary` in [WidgetIntents.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataruWidgets/WidgetIntents.swift:24), und Xcode markiert solche Einträge gelegentlich als stale.

Wenn du willst, lasse ich diesen `xcstrings`-Diff bewusst **nicht** im Commit (nur Navigation-Fix + Doku), dann bleibt der Commit sauber.

    60	**For users:**
    61	- View device positions with accuracy circles, relative time, and distance.
    62	- Off‑screen arrows point toward devices outside the current map region.
    63	- Optional route navigation shows travel time and progress.
    64	- Pull down to refresh a device’s position, tap arrows to recenter or open another device, and network errors are indicated by an overlay and icon.
    65	
    66	- Off‑screen arrows can display segmented lengths (1 segment per 50 km, up to 10) and are grouped by map edge for clarity. Their visibility is controlled by a global setting.
    67	- When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.
    68	- Navigation includes a scale bar and custom compass; auto‑centering pauses while you interact and resumes automatically once idle.
    69	- Route progress can be visualized using completed vs. remaining segments with a moving ghost marker (shown after at least 5% estimated progress).
    70	- Routes are recalculated when transport mode changes or after significant movement; route requests are rate‑limited daily, and the reload action can force a fresh calculation ignoring caches.
    71	- Start navigation by long‑pressing a device pin on the map or swiping right on a device row. Your own device never offers navigation. Apple Maps handoff uses proper destination names.
    72	- When you switch navigation to route from your device toward a selected device, a top overlay displays turn‑by‑turn instructions.
    73	
    74	**For developers:**
    75	- `iPhone_DeviceMapView` draws markers, off‑screen arrows, error overlays, network‑error icons, and handles map camera logic, timers, and edit/navigation sheets. Auto‑centering gating is unified across views.
    76	- `iPhone_DeviceNavigationView` uses `MKRoute`, `RouteCacheStore`, and `SettingsManager.navigationTransportType` to render routes and progress; it recalculates on transport changes or movement thresholds and enforces a daily route‑request limit.
    77	- `NavigationOverlayKit` is used in `iPhone_DeviceNavigationView` to show live turn‑by‑turn instructions when routing from the current device toward the target device.
    78	- `RouteGhostCalculator` estimates remote progress along the route using last update timestamps and current/estimated speed; progress overlay rendering splits polylines into completed/remaining segments.
    79	- `MapScaleBar` is backed by `MapScaleBarViewModel` for cached updates; `MapCompass` is shared.
    80	- `OffscreenDeviceEdgeHelper` groups arrow indicators by edge and scales coordinates; segments represent ~50 km and are capped at 10.
    81	- `MiataruMapMarker` and label components use rasterized caching keyed by color/icon/height/colorScheme/scale and respect Dynamic Type and color scheme.
    82	
    83	## QR Code Sharing
    84	**For users:**
    85	- Display your own device ID as a QR code, copy it, or share via link or email.
    86	- Add other devices by scanning their Miataru QR code.
    87	- The QR tab offers one‑tap sharing, shows visitor history directly below your code, and the add‑device sheet guides scanning and rejects non‑Miataru codes.
    88	
    89	- The share sheet includes additional options, and email sharing attaches the QR image reliably.
    90	
    91	**For developers:**
    92	- `iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView` renders customizable QR codes using the `QRCode` package and supports `ShareLink` and `MFMailComposeViewController`.
    93	- `VisitorHistoryViewModel` and `VisitorHistorySection` power inline visitor history within the QR tab, while `iPhone_VisitorHistoryView` reuses the same data loader.
    94	- `iPhone_AddDeviceView` validates the `miataru://` prefix from scanned codes before accepting an ID and allows manual entry with color selection.

Output:
     1	version 3.1.2
     2	- Removed deprecated `UIViewController.attemptRotationToDeviceOrientation()` usage from rotation-lock handling and relied on scene/controller orientation update APIs (`setNeedsUpdateOfSupportedInterfaceOrientations` + geometry updates) to keep iOS 16+ builds warning-free.
     3	- Prioritized local on-device position updates in focused double-tap navigation by introducing an unfiltered raw location stream for immediate camera/overlay updates instead of waiting on sensitivity-filtered location acceptance.
     4	- Fixed focused-navigation heading arrow update cadence by subscribing the navigation view to raw local location updates, reducing situations where the arrow appeared to follow stale/server-driven movement.
     5	- Reduced heading-arrow jitter in simulator/low-quality heading scenarios by preferring smoothed heading values and only falling back to smoothed course data when compass accuracy is not reliable.
     6	- Incremented iOS app build number (`CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION`) from 7 to 8.
     7	- Stabilized focused double-tap navigation camera framing so the own device marker remains visible in the lower screen area at low speed/standstill instead of drifting to or below the bottom edge.
     8	- Reduced follow-camera look-ahead aggressiveness and made heading fallback logic more defensive in reversed navigation mode to avoid premature off-screen positioning before movement speed increases.
     9	- Added arrival clock time to the active-navigation route info accessory (`… • <ETA> • <localized prefix>: <time>`), derived from remaining route duration.
    10	- Added full localization for the arrival prefix across all supported app languages (`de`: `Ankunft`, `en`: `ETA`, plus da/es/fi/fr/it/ja/nl/zh-Hans).
    11	- Fixed `scripts/test-screenshots.sh` selector parsing for `set -u` shells by making empty-array loops nounset-safe (`"${array[@]-}"`), preventing crashes like `selected_inputs[@]: unbound variable` when no `--test` selectors are passed.

# Vollmodus Route und Live ETA (2026-02-19 17:12Z)

_**User**_

wenn der benutzer per doppel-tap in den vollständigen Navigationsmodus wechselt soll die route zuverlässig angezeigt werden. Das heisst es soll auch kein ghost mehr in diesem Modus angezeigt werden sondern nur die route und überlagerung wenn mutually-active.

Aktuell kommt es noch in diesem navigationsmodus während der navigation zu problemen bei der routen-darstellung auf der karte (mal fehlt sie, besonders wenn mutually-active den status wechselt zwischen active und nicht active)

---

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_

Umgesetzt:
- Fokus-Navigationsmodus (Double-Tap) rendert jetzt stabil nur noch die Basisroute.
- Ghost/Progress-Segmentierung wird in diesem Modus nicht mehr gezeichnet.
- Mutual-Navigation-Overlay bleibt aktiv und wird weiterhin korrekt über die Route gelegt.
- Build-Check für das Projekt war erfolgreich.

---

_**User**_

Ich habe ein weiteres Problem identifiziert. In diesem Modus wird leider, wenn der Route immer gefolgt wird, nicht regelmässig die ETA/Entfernung in dem Bottom Overlay aktualisiert.

---

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_

Erweitert:
- Kontinuierliche Aktualisierung von ETA und Distanz im fokussierten Navigationsmodus.
- Berechnung der Restdistanz entlang der aktiven Route (`route.polyline.remainingDistance`).
- Interpolierte Restzeit basierend auf verbleibender Distanz und `expectedTravelTime`.
- Updates werden bei Positionsänderungen und zusätzlich im 1-Sekunden-Takt angewendet.
- Nach Route-Refresh (neu berechnet oder Cache) werden die Werte sofort auf Basis der neuen Route synchronisiert.

---

_**User**_

wenn die route zwischenzeitlich aktualisiert wird, dann funktioniert das eta update dann auch immer mit der dann aktualisierten route/auf basis dieser neuen route?

---

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_

Bestätigt:
- ETA/Distanz nutzen immer die aktuell gesetzte Route.
- Nach Route-Refresh werden die Werte sofort neu gesetzt und danach live weitergeführt.

---

_**User**_

wenn der nutzer sich nicht bewegt, müsste dann die eta nicht "steigen"?

---

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_

Klarstellung:
- Aktuelle Logik ist distanzbasiert interpoliert.
- Bei Stillstand bleibt die Restzeit dadurch weitgehend konstant.
- Nutzer hat festgelegt, dass eine weitere Anpassung hierfür vorerst nicht notwendig ist.

---

_**User**_

erst einmal nicht notwendig, ich komme später vielleicht darauf zurück.

dokumentiere, beschreibe und committe alles

---

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_

Dokumentation und Commit vorbereitet:
- `CHANGELOG.md` auf `version 3.1` ergänzt (Routing-Stabilität und Live-ETA im Vollmodus).
- Diese `.specstory`-History-Datei erstellt.
- Alle aktuellen Änderungen zusammen staged und committed.

 ### Navigation Route Refresh Behavior
 - Auto-refresh route decisions are centralized in `views/Common/NavigationRouteRefreshPolicy.swift`.
 - Hard refresh triggers: auto-update enabled + missing route, or user off-route.
 - Standard navigation mode (`isRouteFromDeviceToUser == true`): target movement only triggers reroute when target moved significantly **and** is off the current route.
 - Reverse navigation mode keeps movement-trigger behavior compatible with prior logic after the significant-movement check.
 - Route reuse still goes through `RouteCacheStore` (`useCachedRouteIfValid`) before issuing new `MKDirections` requests.
+- Focused double-tap navigation mode (`isNavigationMode == true`) intentionally renders a stable base route (plus optional mutual-navigation overlay) without ghost/progress segmentation.
+- Focused mode periodically re-establishes the already-available route polyline on the map (~6s cadence) to prevent transient disappearing overlays; this is a render refresh and does **not** trigger additional `MKDirections` API calls.

 version 3.1.2

 - Fixed focused-navigation heading arrow update cadence by subscribing the navigation view to raw local location updates, reducing situations where the arrow appeared to follow stale/server-driven movement.

 - When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.
 - Navigation includes a scale bar and custom compass; auto‑centering pauses while you interact and resumes automatically once idle.

+- In focused double-tap navigation mode, ghost/progress segmentation is intentionally disabled; the app renders the stable base route (and optional mutual-navigation overlay) and periodically re-establishes that overlay locally without extra route API requests.
 - Routes are recalculated when transport mode changes or after significant movement; route requests are rate‑limited daily, and the reload action can force a fresh calculation ignoring caches.
 - Start navigation by long‑pressing a device pin on the map or swiping right on a device row. Your own device never offers navigation. Apple Maps handoff uses proper destination names.
 - When you switch navigation to route from your device toward a selected device, a top overlay displays turn‑by‑turn instructions.

 version 3.1.2
+- Re-established route polyline rendering in focused double-tap navigation mode on a short cadence (~6s) to prevent occasional map overlay disappearance; this refresh re-renders the existing route and does not trigger additional `MKDirections` requests.
+- Ensured focused double-tap navigation consistently suppresses ghost/progress visuals (including residual green progress segments) and renders only the base route plus optional mutual-navigation overlay.
+- Changed widget intent `parameterSummary` to key-path form (`Summary { \.$device }`) and removed obsolete `"Show ${device}"` localization content to prevent stale string-catalog entries in `miataruWidgets/Localizable.xcstrings`.
 - Removed deprecated `UIViewController.attemptRotationToDeviceOrientation()` usage from rotation-lock handling and relied on scene/controller orientation update APIs (`setNeedsUpdateOfSupportedInterfaceOrientations` + geometry updates) to keep iOS 16+ builds warning-free.
 - Prioritized local on-device position updates in focused double-tap navigation by introducing an unfiltered raw location stream for immediate camera/overlay updates instead of waiting on sensitivity-filtered location acceptance.
 - Fixed focused-navigation heading arrow update cadence by subscribing the navigation view to raw local location updates, reducing situations where the arrow appeared to follow stale/server-driven movement.
diff --git a/miataru/DEVELOPMENT.md b/miataru/DEVELOPMENT.md

--- a/miataru/DEVELOPMENT.md
+++ b/miataru/DEVELOPMENT.md
@@ -80,6 +80,11 @@ miataru/
 - Standard navigation mode (`isRouteFromDeviceToUser == true`): target movement only triggers reroute when target moved significantly **and** is off the current route.
 - Reverse navigation mode keeps movement-trigger behavior compatible with prior logic after the significant-movement check.
 - Route reuse still goes through `RouteCacheStore` (`useCachedRouteIfValid`) before issuing new `MKDirections` requests.
+- Focused double-tap navigation mode (`isNavigationMode == true`) intentionally renders a stable base route (plus optional mutual-navigation overlay) without ghost/progress segmentation.
+- Focused mode periodically re-establishes the already-available route polyline on the map (~6s cadence) to prevent transient disappearing overlays; this is a render refresh and does **not** trigger additional `MKDirections` API calls.
+
+### Widget Intent String Extraction
+- `DeviceSelectionIntent.parameterSummary` uses key-path summary syntax (`Summary { \.$device }`) to avoid generating a fragile interpolated key (`"Show ${device}"`) that can become stale in `miataruWidgets/Localizable.xcstrings`.
